cluster_name: India Cockroach Janta Party protests force Education Minister Pradhan resignation
tldr: The headline layer is dominated by a POLITICAL accountability frame, with nine of thirteen buckets anchoring homepage coverage to the minister-resignation or Modi-pressure angle — a narrower, harder focus than body text sustains, where the education-system failure and police-violence frames each receive more independent space. BBC World stands alone in foregrounding documentary evidence at the title level ('Videos show officers firing pellet guns'), shifting from the political-contest framing shared by almost every other outlet to a state-behavior framing grounded in visual evidence. International explainer outlets (El Pais, AFP) make movement identity the headline hook — asking 'Who are the cockroaches?' and 'Why are India's youth protesting?' — diverging sharply from the demand-centered, resignation-outcome framing of Indian, Pakistani, and Canadian press. The Diplomat is the only outlet whose headline invokes the Gandhi civil-disobedience lineage, embedding a historical-analytical frame that suppresses both the resignation outcome and the political pressure narrative visible in all other Asia-Pacific-adjacent outlets.
event_summary: India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement, protesting the NEET exam paper leak, held 36 days of demonstrations at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi; Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following police clashes that injured at least 180 people.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the corpus to foreground documentary evidence of police conduct ('Videos show officers firing pellet guns') rather than merely reporting the crackdown as an allegation or narrative — making state violence verifiable-looking at the RSS/homepage layer where all other outlets rely on descriptive assertion.

Only headline to frame the protest through historical civil-disobedience tradition ('Born in Jails, Popularized by Gandhi, Hunger Strikes Can Hit Authorities Hard') — a meta-analytical frame suppressing the resignation outcome and political pressure narrative visible in every other outlet's title.

Only outlet to use 'fiasco' in the headline ('NEET leak fiasco'), the most editorially charged descriptor in the corpus; all other outlets use neutral markers ('paper leak', 'exam fraud') that withhold editorial judgement at the title level.

Only headline to characterize the government's negotiating posture as 'seeks time' rather than 'promises', 'responds', or 'acts' — framing governmental delay as the news event rather than Modi's pledges, a construction absent from all other international outlets.

Only headline — in any language — to deploy the rhetorical move framing Modi as historically superseded ('Narendra Modi is the past, he cannot fight the future'), a generational-replacement narrative compressed into the title that English-language outlets express only in body text if at all.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, nearly every outlet collapses this story to the POLITICAL accountability register — minister resignation, Modi under pressure, opposition solidarity — crowding out the education-policy failure and police-violence narratives that body text distributes more evenly across frames; BBC World's pellet-gun video headline is the only title to anchor state behavior in evidence rather than allegation. International explainer outlets asking 'who are the cockroaches?' and 'why is India's youth protesting?' treat movement identity as the primary hook, diverging sharply from the resignation-outcome and ultimatum framing of South Asian and Canadian press — a headline-level divergence the sensationalism index will capture as a body–headline gap in framing register.
